patch.summary:
Choose Bitbucket Cloud only if your buying job matches “Atlassian git hosting — Free ≤5 users; Standard $3.65/user/mo (min 5-user equivalent); Pre” rather than incident.io's shape. Choose incident.io only if your buying job matches “Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-ca” rather than Bitbucket Cloud's shape. Workflow advantage: Bitbucket Cloud leans source-control-devops; incident.io leans incident-oncall. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Bitbucket Cloud is Atlassian git hosting — Free ≤5 users; Standard $3.65/user/mo (min 5-user equivalent); Premium $7.25/user/mo.; incident.io is Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/user; on-call add-on +$10–$20/user. Does not outrank PagerDut.
- Company-size focus: Bitbucket Cloud (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs incident.io (small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Bitbucket Cloud-leaning source-control-devops vs incident.io-leaning incident-oncall.
- Researched limits: Bitbucket Cloud — Paid plans bill a 5-user floor even for 2-person teams; incident.io — On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor.

Limitations — Bitbucket Cloud: Paid plans bill a 5-user floor even for 2-person teams; Ecosystem and Actions marketplace trail GitHub; incident.io: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor; Does not outrank PagerDuty (8.0) as the incident-oncall award.

Poor-fit cases: Bitbucket Cloud is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Paid plans bill a 5-user floor even for 2-person teams · incident.io is a poor fit when that limitation bites: On-call paging is an add-on (+$10–$20/user), not included in the $15 Team floor · Avoid Bitbucket Cloud if you actually need incident.io's motion (Incident response — Basic Free; Team $15/user/mo annual ($19 monthly); Pro $25/u)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
